jobs.title: Manager, Operations
jobs.description:
Xcel Energy (NASDAQ: XEL) is a leading energy provider and Fortune 500 company, dedicated to serving millions of electricity and natural gas customers across eight states: Minnesota, Colorado, Wisconsin, Michigan, North Dakota, South Dakota, New Mexico and Texas. We make energy work better for our customers, helping them thrive every day. That means always raising the bar - delivering better service and providing more reliable, resilient, and sustainable energy.

Xcel Energy is a place where you’ll have opportunities to grow, expand your skills, and help lead the clean energy transition. We offer meaningful rewards, recognition, and support to help you build your career and make an impact - both on the job and beyond. Most importantly, it means you’ll be joining a company that knows employees are the driving force behind its success and is committed to helping you be your best.

Xcel Energy supports a hybrid work model to enable collaboration and flexibility. Many roles are expected to work onsite three days per week (Tuesday–Thursday); however, work location expectations vary based on role, team, and business needs.
Position Summary

Standard Operations Position. Supervise a high performing, safe operations team across multiple functions, facilities, or commodities while driving the efficient and cost-effective use of numerous resources through consistent and effective application of policies and procedures. Assure safe, reliable, and compliant operations, drive continuous improvement, and ensure customer satisfaction. Drive attainment of corporate and business unit strategies, goals and objectives, and process and performance metrics.

This position works on site at the Sagamore Wind Farm Mon-Fri.

Essential Responsibilities
- Provide visible safety leadership and actively contribute to the creation, implementation, and continuous improvement of a strong, sustainable safety culture in partnership with Safety Consultant. Drive real time safety accountability by engaging the team through safety meeting participation, job briefs, audits, training, accident investigation/event assessment, and job site observations.
- Business Optimization & Strategy: Evaluate team performance based on operational efficiency, reliability and quality metrics and take corrective action where appropriate, focusing on process adherence and data integrity. Identify continuous improvement opportunities and drive adoption of process changes through effective collaboration and expectation setting.
- Operational Effectiveness: Provide direct leadership over crew effectiveness, quality and productivity. Maintain a continuous presence in the work environment and assist in removing barriers with pre-requisites, materials, stakeholder, and other issues. Ensure correct crew composition and skills are in place to meet operational, reliability, customer and financial objectives. Assist in preparing resource forecasts and providing input to longer-term work plans.
- Talent Management: Recruit talented employees, participate in workforce and development planning efforts, establish clear expectations, and effectively and manage performance. Provide training, coaching and oversight and drive employee engagement. Effectively represent the organization in bargaining unit discussions, grievances, corrective actions and development.
- Relationship Management: Build and maintain effective internal and external relationships with areas that support Operations. Provide strong working knowledge of necessary systems and resources to assist employees, other work groups, and/or customers and stakeholders. Enable crews to provide solutions to issues and improve customer/stakeholder satisfaction.
- Regulatory & Compliance: Oversee and coordinate the execution and documentation of work in accordance with Xcel Energy policies and procedures, labor agreements, and regulatory standards. Support and ensure required compliance and technical training is completed. Establish, monitor, and track processes to ensure regulatory compliance.

Minimum Requirements

- Five or more years in design, construction, operations, engineering or maintenance of utility systems/power generation plants or related industries/fields or equivalent.
- Associates or technical degree preferred.
- Demonstrated technical expertise in specific functional area including standards, procedures, and applicable government/environmental regulations.
- Operational knowledge of work and asset management and analytical/reporting applications.
- Effective change leader with demonstrated ability to effectively communicate company and business area strategies and objectives to a variety of stakeholders.
- Proven results at achieving performance and operational metrics and driving process adherence.

Preferred Experience, Skills, and Abilities
- Three years of supervisory experience.
- Completion of an approved apprentice program in an appropriately related craft.
- Demonstrated understanding of utility finance.
- Demonstrated experience working as or with bargaining unit employees.
- Will be required to work rotating shifts and/or be on call.
- Live within a 60-mile proximity of work location Sagamore Wind Farm

Our culture is grounded in shared values and employee commitments that guide how we work, support one another, and grow together.

Our Values
Connected, Committed, Trustworthy, Safe

Our Employee Commitments
- Work that makes a difference
- A team you can count of
- Opportunities to grow
- Rewards that help you thrive

- Three years supervisory experience.
- Knowledge of and demonstrated ability to administer/work within union labor agreements.
- Operational knowledge of work and asset management and analytical/reporting applications.
- Ability to effectively communicate and lead company and business area strategies and objectives.
- Proven results at setting, driving performance and operational metrics and achieving process adherence.
- Will be required to be on call for escalated operations and emergencies.

jobs.title: Director of Transformation Technology Delivery, Integrations Lead
jobs.description:
Xcel Energy (NASDAQ: XEL) is a leading energy provider and Fortune 500 company, dedicated to serving millions of electricity and natural gas customers across eight states: Minnesota, Colorado, Wisconsin, Michigan, North Dakota, South Dakota, New Mexico and Texas. We make energy work better for our customers, helping them thrive every day. That means always raising the bar - delivering better service and providing more reliable, resilient, and sustainable energy.

Xcel Energy is a place where you’ll have opportunities to grow, expand your skills, and help lead the clean energy transition. We offer meaningful rewards, recognition, and support to help you build your career and make an impact - both on the job and beyond. Most importantly, it means you’ll be joining a company that knows employees are the driving force behind its success and is committed to helping you be your best.

Xcel Energy supports a hybrid work model to enable collaboration and flexibility. Many roles are expected to work onsite three days per week (Tuesday–Thursday); however, work location expectations vary based on role, team, and business needs.

Position Summary:

The Customer Core Integration Delivery Lead is the accountable Xcel Energy leader for integration delivery across the program. This role owns both halves of the integration picture: the SAP integrations built on BTP, and the integration and application remediation required for edge systems that connect to the new CIS.

The Director of Transformation Technology Delivery is responsible for leading the day-to-day execution of technology delivery within major transformation programs. The role oversees planning, coordination, and delivery across multiple technology domains, ensuring that solutions are built, tested, and deployed in alignment with program objectives, regulatory timelines, and enterprise standards.

This position partners closely with IT operations, business readiness, change management, architecture, PMO, and vendor teams to ensure integrated delivery and successful transition to ongoing support. The Director provides both strategic and tactical leadership across delivery teams, manages program risks and issues, and ensures value realization through disciplined execution and effective stakeholder engagement.

Essential Responsibilities:

- Partner with integration architects to apply the approved integration strategy, ISA-M patterns and clean-core principles, and make sure every interface has a clear pattern decision (application-to-application, B2B, API-managed or event-driven).
- Drive integration monitoring, error handling and alerting standards so that interfaces are operable on day one, not just functional.
- Lead delivery of integration and application remediation for retained edge applications.
- Coordinate remediation across enterprise middleware and API platforms, including ACE/APIC, SeeBurger, MFT, IICS, and customer APIs on Apigee and AWS services.
- Plan and govern integration shutdown and recommissioning for edge applications scheduled for retirement once the new CIS becomes the system of record.
- Build and maintain an integrated integration delivery plan that aligns BTP and edge work to the program release roadmap, test cycles, freeze periods and customer experience protection windows.
- Hold the system integrator and vendors accountable for scope, quality, schedule and estimates; review deliverables and resolve escalations.
- Own integration risks, issues, dependencies and decisions, and report status, readiness and trade-offs clearly to program and IT leadership.
- Coordinate closely with architecture, data conversion, testing, security, infrastructure and network teams, and with business process owners.
- Develop and mentor Xcel Energy integration staff and contractors so that integration capability remains in-house after go-live.

Minimum Requirements:

- Bachelor’s degree in Business, Technology, Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.
- 10+ years of experience in IT program delivery, systems implementation, technology operations, or utility-focused IT roles with minimum 5 years of leadership experience.
- Demonstrated experience delivering large-scale or multi-tower technology initiatives.
- Strong understanding of integrated utility systems, modernization, and cross-platform delivery practices.
- Proven ability to manage both internal and vendor delivery teams in a matrixed environment.
- Strong problem-solving skills, with ability to resolve issues in complex, fast-moving program environments.
- Effective communication and stakeholder management skills, with ability to translate delivery needs for business partners.

Preferred Requirements:

- Hands-on delivery experience with API management and event-driven patterns.
- Working knowledge of enterprise middleware and API platforms such as IBM ACE/APIC, Apigee, AWS integration services, MFT and B2B/EDI tools.
- Proven ability to manage system integrator and vendor delivery, including scope, estimates, quality gates and escalations.
- Clear, direct communication with both technical teams and senior leaders.
- Utility industry experience, particularly with meter-to-cash processes and applications.

jobs.description:
Are you looking for an exciting job where you can put your skills and talents to work at a company you can feel proud to be a part of? Do you want a workplace that will challenge you and offer you opportunities to learn and grow?  A   position at Xcel Energy could be just what you’re looking for.

At Xcel Energy, our employees are the driving force behind our success. So we make sure that, here, you can be your best. Doing work that makes a difference for neighbors and communities. Working with a team you can count on to push you. Expanding skills, staying ready for change, and capturing opportunities to grow. All with the support, rewards and recognition you need to thrive – during your internship and beyond.

The intern will support the Energy Supply Strategy, Governance, and Business Operations organization. This team serves as a central coordination function for Energy Supply, providing business planning, governance, and executive communications coordination across the business. The organization works closely with senior leaders to improve visibility to priorities, support organizational effectiveness, enhance communication practices, and drive continuous improvement initiatives.

The intern will help develop and execute communications that keep employees informed and aligned with business priorities. Responsibilities may include supporting leadership presentations, creating communication and marketing materials, maintaining SharePoint content, assisting with employee engagement activities, documenting business processes, reviewing workflows for improvement opportunities, and supporting recurring reporting and governance activities. The position offers exposure to executive communications, business planning, performance reporting, change management, and cross-functional collaboration within a complex utility environment.

- Assist in developing and distributing internal communications, announcements, newsletters, and employee engagement materials.

- Create and update presentations, executive briefing materials, infographics, and other visual communication tools.

- Support SharePoint site maintenance, content development, and communication resource management.

- Review and document business processes, identify improvement opportunities, and assist with process standardization efforts.

- Support business operations activities including reporting, meeting coordination, action tracking, and governance documentation.

This position is for a May 24, 2027 start date. This position may have the possibility to extend beyond the internship’s initial term based on the candidate’s successful performance and Xcel Energy’s business needs.

Establish and direct the execution of coordinated strategies that align long-term planning, regulatory, and commercial objectives to deliver reliable, affordable, executable and cost-effective outcomes.

Serve as a company representative in industry, regulatory, customer and policy forums. Shape external planning and policy frameworks, build stakeholder alignment, and advance approval, cost allocation, and cost recovery strategies for major infrastructure investments, in alignment with company priorities.

Anticipate and identify emerging risks and opportunities related to system planning, policy changes, and large load growth, and mobilize internal and external stakeholders to advance enterprise and operating-company objectives.

Essential Responsibilities

- Own the identification, prioritization, and strategic response to emerging policy, market, regulatory, and system-planning issues that materially affect long-term infrastructure investment, reliability, customer growth, or cost recovery.
- Serve as a company representative and strategic spokesperson with regulators, Commissioners, federal agencies, RTO leadership, customers, municipalities, market participants, peer utilities, and/or policy stakeholders, cultivating strong relationships.
- Influence external policy, market, and planning frameworks to advance company priorities and mitigate material regulatory, financial, reliability, and customer risks.
- Establish and govern integrated planning strategies across generation, transmission, distribution, customer-driven growth, and other long-range system needs. Translate complex planning and market insights into clear recommendations for executive leadership.
- Develop and execute strategies for planning policy, cost allocation, and cost recovery across applicable regulatory frameworks. Accountable for responses to regulatory proceedings, policy changes, and stakeholder initiatives impacting system planning and investment.
- Provide expert written and oral testimony in regulatory proceedings on issues that impact cost of service, generation resource needs, or transmission needs.
- Build and lead a high-performing multidisciplinary team, establishing priorities, performance expectations, resource strategies, workforce capabilities, succession plans, and accountability for results.
- Oversee development of contracts, agreements, and partnerships supporting planning and investment strategies.

Minimum Requirements

- Bachelor’s degree in business, economics, finance, engineering, or related discipline. Master's degree preferred.
- 12 years of utility experience.

Preferred Requirements
- Experience in state or federal regulatory affairs, system planning, engineering, markets, or public policy.

The Business Transformation Intern will support the Customer Core (CIS Modernization) program within the Products & Services Tower at Xcel Energy, based in Minneapolis, MN. As the program transitions into detailed design, development, and training preparation, the intern will work alongside business leads, product owners, and cross-functional tower teams (e.g., billing, reporting, and customer experience) to help translate business requirements into actionable deliverables. This includes supporting process design documentation, identifying gaps (e.g., non-SAP integration considerations), and preparing materials that enable successful system build, testing, and end-user training. The intern will gain exposure to large-scale utility transformation, regulatory considerations, and how business, technology, and data teams collaborate to deliver customer-focused outcomes. Work will be performed in a hybrid environment based in Minneapolis or Denver, with frequent interaction across distributed teams.

Typical intern responsibilities may include but are not limited to:
- Support development and refinement of detailed business process designs and documentation as the program moves into design and build phases

- Analyze and organize requirements, decisions, and dependencies across towers, including tracking gaps (e.g., non-SAP solutions, cross-system integrations)

- Assist in creation of training and change management materials to support future system adoption (job aids, process guides, presentations)

- Coordinate inputs from product owners, SMEs, and tower leads to ensure alignment across customer, billing, and reporting workstreams

- Support program reporting and organization needs, including preparing summaries, tracking action items, and maintaining documentation repositories

- Contribute to continuous improvement by identifying inefficiencies or risks in current processes and proposing structured solutions

jobs.title: Emergency Response Program Manager
jobs.description:
Xcel Energy (NASDAQ: XEL) is a leading energy provider and Fortune 500 company, dedicated to serving millions of electricity and natural gas customers across eight states: Minnesota, Colorado, Wisconsin, Michigan, North Dakota, South Dakota, New Mexico and Texas. We make energy work better for our customers, helping them thrive every day. That means always raising the bar - delivering better service and providing more reliable, resilient, and sustainable energy.

Xcel Energy is a place where you’ll have opportunities to grow, expand your skills, and help lead the clean energy transition. We offer meaningful rewards, recognition, and support to help you build your career and make an impact - both on the job and beyond. Most importantly, it means you’ll be joining a company that knows employees are the driving force behind its success and is committed to helping you be your best.

Xcel Energy supports a hybrid work model to enable collaboration and flexibility. Many roles are expected to work onsite three days per week (Tuesday–Thursday); however, work location expectations vary based on role, team, and business needs.
Position Summary

The Emergency Response Program Manager governs the emergency response program, including plan lifecycle management, hazard and risk assessments, training, drills, and corrective actions. The role partners with Operations Managers to maintain site Emergency Action Plans for existing facilities and develop plans for renewables and emerging generation technologies. It also works with internal and external stakeholders to strengthen and sustain enterprise response capabilities. This program role does not replace site operational command or the technical authority of Safety, Environmental, Security, or Engineering.

Essential Responsibilities

- Govern fleet emergency-preparedness standards, procedures, records, and annual work plan. Coordinate annual EAP reviews, lead all-hazards assessments, and integrate results into plans, training, exercises, and mitigation actions.
- Provide technical leadership to site Emergency Plan stakeholders, lead process improvements, and manage major emergency-planning projects through design and implementation.
- Apply advanced emergency-planning expertise to resolve issues, define methods, and improve program approaches across related assignments.
- Establish preparedness metrics, assess program performance, report risks and lessons learned, and track corrective actions to closure.
- Support emergency-planning needs for acquisitions, new builds, technology changes, and construction-to-operations handoffs.
- Define role-based NIMS/ICS training requirements and maintain completion records.
- Participate in external emergency-planning forums, represent the fleet as a subject matter expert, and support related training.

Minimum Requirements

- Bachelor’s degree in engineering, science, emergency management, or business-related field is required.
- Ten years of progressive experience in emergency preparedness, electric utility operations, or incident management is required.
- Strong knowledge of utility operations and ICS/NIMS required. Certified Emergency Manager (CEM), PMP, or similar advanced credential preferred.

Preferred Experience & Skills:
- Experience developing or governing emergency response programs across multiple sites, asset types, or operating companies.
- Experience supporting emergency response for conventional thermal generation plants, renewable generation, emerging technologies, or new builds.
